title: The Contingent Anchor
subtitle: Regime dependence in gold's sensitivity to real interest rates, 2003–2026
overview: Gold is supposed to move against real interest rates. I wanted to know whether that relationship has always held — and it hasn't.
credit: Co-authored with faculty supervisor Dr. Kapil Tomar (CSE, TIET), in standard IEEE conference format. Full draft largely complete — targeting IMRC 2026 (IIM Ahmedabad) and ConfAI 2026 (Plaksha University). Outstanding: rebuilding Table I, restyling figures, and finalising references.
body: Gold is supposed to move inversely with real interest rates — but is that relationship actually stable, or does it switch by regime? And what explains gold's large, unexplained run-up since 2022?

The dataset is weekly, about 1,226 observations from 2003 to mid-2026, pulled together from FRED (real yields, breakevens, VIX, WTI), Yahoo Finance (gold, dollar, silver, copper), the Caldara–Iacoviello geopolitical risk index, and IMF/WGC demand data.

Structural-break testing turns up a robust break at January 2009: before it, gold's beta to real rates is positive (+2.90); after, it's negative (−6.03) — the textbook negative relationship doesn't predate quantitative easing, it emerges with it.

The harder finding is the one I kept trying to explain away. A block-bootstrap on the post-2022 drift turns up +80.5% that the model can't explain, beating all 5,000 resamples (p < 0.0002). I ran a copper placebo as a sanity check — it came back clean and insignificant, which tells me the method isn't just manufacturing residuals out of noise.

Layering on XGBoost with rolling SHAP attribution gave a result I liked precisely because it was uncomfortable: explanatory R² falls from 0.32 to 0.10 post-2022, while the model leans more heavily on the real-rate feature, not less. That's a genuine tension, not a tidy story.

The paper reports its nulls honestly too — regime dummies don't improve forecasts, and the central-bank holdings data became unusable once Russia stopped reporting to the IMF, in exactly the month the anomaly begins.
